newsitem.title: USA: Sprint Spectrum junk bonds jump on buyout rumor.
newsitem.headline: Sprint Spectrum junk bonds jump on buyout rumor.

text.p: The junk bonds of Sprint Spectrum L.P., jumped roughly two percent in value on Thursday on a rumor that Sprint Corp was moving to increase its 40 percent stake in the personal communications services (PCS) provider.
Comments made by Tele-Communications Inc chairman John Malone on Thursday added to the speculation that Sprint Spctrum may be in play.

Speaking at a major cable trade show on the West coast, Malone said TCI needed to refocus on increasing earnings from its core business. That comment led bond traders to believe that TCI may consider selling its 30 percent stake in Sprint Spectrum.
A spokeswoman for TCI said, "It wouldn't be appropriate to say what changes the future may hold. TCI is looking at all of the areas and costs within the company."
A spokesman for Sprint Inc said the company as a policy does not comment on rumors.

As a result of the speculation, bids on Sprint Spectrum zero coupon bonds rose to 68 1/2 from 65, and bids on its 11 percent senior notes rose to 108 from 105 in trading on Thursday, market sources said.
Traders said total trading volume was well over $80 million.
Sprint Spectrum has a total of $750 million of junk bonds outstanding.
Market players speculated the B2/B-plus rating of the bonds may be upgraded if Sprint Inc, which has a higher credit rating than Sprint Spectrum, increases its 40 percent stake in the company.
